mark1.anim.capture: Add this face as a frame
mark1.anim.hint: Capture the face as a frame, build up a sequence, and play it back here or on the device. Frames hold the mouth drawing and every eye LED.

mark1.fw.started: Building the firmware on the device, then flashing it. This takes a few minutes.
mark1.fw.typePrompt: Updating the firmware rewrites the faceplate board. If it is interrupted the eyes and mouth stop working until it is run again. Do not power the device off while it runs. Type UPDATE to continue:
mark1.fw.current: Running version {running}. This is the current firmware.
mark1.fw.notReported: The board has not reported its firmware version yet.
mark1.fw.unknown: The firmware version could not be read.
mark1.fw.hint: The eyes and the mouth are driven by a small board with its own firmware, separate from the OVOS software. It rarely needs changing.
mark1.fw.title: Faceplate firmware
mark1.live.on: Following the device. The eyes show what the Mark-1 is showing.
mark1.live.off: Showing your design. The device is not being read.
mark1.canvas.aria: Mark-1 faceplate: left eye ring, mouth matrix, right eye ring
mark1.intro: Design the Mark-1's eyes and mouth, preview them right here in the browser, and send the result to a real device.
mark1.unconfirmed: The panel could not confirm a Mark-1. It asks the faceplate for its eye colour and its firmware version, and only a recent ovos-PHAL-plugin-mk1 answers those, so a working Mark-1 can stay silent here. The controls below still send, but nothing reports back whether the faceplate acted on them.
mark1.simulator.title: Simulator
mark1.simulator.hint: This preview runs entirely in your browser. It works even without a Mark-1 connected — use it to design before you send anything to the device.
mark1.mouth.title: Mouth
mark1.mouth.hint: Click or drag on the grid above to draw. Each lamp is one pixel of the mouth display (8 rows by 32 columns).
